text: Design (no code) a Socratic plan review, written to docs/design/socratic-review.md. It serves the BRIEF.md addendum '2026-10-14: Socratic questions', the 2026-10-13 addendum's 'good questions that generate good defaults', A1 (pushes back, open questions), A2-4 (mispredictions update defaults, estimates and routing), A3 (lessons from corrections turned into context, checks and examples) and A6-4 (Jev for rubric checks and gates). After a reading and before dispatch, Athena asks the plan questions of fixed kinds: assumptions, evidence the verifier can observe, file boundaries, decomposition, consistency of scope with deliverables, and root cause versus symptom. Answer each from the cheapest source first: facts from code, records or the host (for example 'does this repository allow merge commits?'), then Jev as a typed question with a probability, and only the residue goes to the user, ranked by how likely the answer changes the plan times the cost of being wrong, capped at one or two questions. Record every question and answer; repeated identical answers feed the defaults loop as proposals; a failure that introspection traces to an unasked or wrongly answered question raises that question's weight. Ground it in today's records, citing for each failure the question that would have caught it: D87 (merge commits assumed), 9gwv (criterion the verifier could not observe), 16zf (owner-only BRIEF.md planned), nem8 (design bundled with build), 8qkc and m1bs (scope versus deliverables), the four reader-budget retries, and the 'real repo' claim in PR #59. Also record whether a failure came from the plan, the execution, the verification or the environment, and make acceptance honest ('athena go' without a prompt is not the user's acceptance). Include alternatives, the cost per job, and the reader's token budget.
